Field Notes / Rental guide

Choosing Fencing for Public Works & Flood Repair

Planning a fixed or changing perimeter for repair work in Hamilton and Marion counties.

Request a quoteCall Richard(317) 296-4015

Rental guide · Fence Wizards

Begin with the work boundary

A repair site may run beside an active sidewalk, road, or public property. Share the planned work boundary, pedestrian routes, and equipment access with Richard.

The fencing choice should follow the site plan and project requirements. Identify what will remain fixed and what will change as the work progresses.

When a driven line fits

Post-driven chain link can suit a longer project with a stable perimeter. The posts are driven into the ground and the fabric is tensioned along the line, making it less portable than panels.

It requires suitable ground. Rock, heavy fill, and underground utilities can affect where posts may go and how the line is installed. Share known ground conditions early.

When portable panels help

Panels and weighted stands can be useful on paved surfaces or where the work zone needs to move. Individual sections can be shifted as access changes.

Some projects call for both systems: driven fencing on fixed boundaries and panels in areas that need flexibility. Explain the phases rather than choosing one system for the entire job before discussing the site.

Plan equipment access before the fence

Mark the entry points for excavation equipment, material deliveries, and debris removal. Gate locations matter especially on a driven line, because changes require a crew visit.

If screening is needed along a public-facing edge, include it in the quote. Windscreen changes the load on the supporting fence and should be considered as part of the installation.

Coordinate the schedule and paperwork

Fence Wizards serves Hamilton and Marion counties from Greenwood. Installation normally takes place within 24–48 hours, with emergency timing confirmed directly with Richard.

Ask about insurance certificates required for the job. Quotes include delivery, installation, the agreed rental term, and removal; standard rentals cover up to 12 months.
